BULK UPLOAD TOOLS | USER GUIDE

Bulk Upload User Guide

Internal Transfers and SWIFT Outward Transfers - step by step, with screens

Item Detail
Who should read it Makers, Checkers and Second Checkers (Unit Heads)
Tools covered

1) Internal Transfer Bulk Upload Tool (Flexcube DE upload)

2) SWIFT Outward Bulk Upload Tool (EGP MT103 via RTGS)
Version / date 1.1 - 21 October 2026
Note Screens in this guide are illustrations with sample data. Red numbered circles point to the steps.

1. How the new process works

The same five steps apply to both upload types.

Role Who What they do
Maker Team member Creates the upload in the tool, enters the lines, submits, emails the Checker
Checker A different team member Enters the request again in the tool, runs the check, creates the upload files, emails the Second Checker
Second Checker Unit Head of the function Reviews the request, the files and the Checker's answers; sends for approval; places the files after approval
Approver Egypt Operations DR Approves by email

1.1 Five simple rules

  • Open the tool from the shared folder and click 'Enable Content'.

  • Yellow cells = you type. Grey cells = the tool fills them. You cannot change grey cells.

  • Enter the lines in the SAME ORDER as the request (Maker and Checker). The check compares line 1 with line 1, line 2 with line 2.

  • Paste values only: Ctrl+Alt+V > Values.

  • The tool does not send emails. You send your email yourself from Outlook, replying on the same email chain.

1.2 The status bar

Status shown at the top Meaning Who acts next
NO ACTIVE UPLOAD Nothing in progress Maker
MAKER - DATA ENTRY Lines being entered Maker
SUBMITTED - WAITING FOR CHECKER Maker's lines are locked Checker
CHECK PASSED - READY TO CREATE FILES All lines matched Checker
UPLOAD FILES CREATED Files ready, batch locked Checker emails the Second Checker

2. Internal Transfers - Maker

Upload sheet - after creating the upload and entering the lines

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Choose the Upload type, Branch code (030 / 033), Batch number and Number of entries from the request.
2 Click 'Create upload'. The tool creates exactly that number of lines (000001, 000002 ...).
3 Fill each yellow line: Account / GL, Account branch (only for a GL of another branch), Narration, D/C, Amount. Typing 8000 becomes 8000.00.
4 Totals update while you type. The Difference must be 0.00.
5 Click 'Submit to Checker'.

2.1 If something is wrong

The submission is rejected and column I tells you exactly what to fix on each line:

Example - branch and GL typed in each other's column, and a comma in the amount

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Put the account or GL number here - not the branch.
2 Branch: 3 digits, only when posting to a GL of another branch. Leave empty otherwise.
3 Read the message, correct the line, click 'Submit to Checker' again.

Message when the upload is not balanced

2.2 When the submission is accepted

Submission accepted - the lines turn grey and are locked

  1. File > Save As > working folder > BulkUpload_<batch>.xlsm (e.g. BulkUpload_5010.xlsm).

  2. Send the email to the Checker from Outlook: attach the original request and write where the workbook is saved. Do not attach the workbook itself.

Email 1 - Maker to Checker (example)

Subject: Bulk Upload - Payroll Files - Batch 5010 - for checking

Dear <Checker>,

Please check the attached request.

Workbook: <working folder>\BulkUpload_5010.xlsm

Upload type / TC: Payroll Files / 097 Branch: 030

Number of entries: 5 Total amount: 23,500.00

Maker: <name>

3. Internal Transfers - Checker

Checker sheet - your own entries from the request, after 'Run check'

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Type (or paste values) every line of the ORIGINAL request, in the same order: Account / GL, Narration, D/C, Amount. You cannot copy from the Maker's sheet.
2 Click 'Run check'.
3 Each line shows 'Matched' (green) or 'DIFFERENT' (red) with the field that differs.
4 When the check has PASSED, click 'Create upload files' and choose the working folder.

You cannot check your own upload

If you are the person who submitted the batch, the tool stops you:

3.1 If a line is different

Example - lines 4 and 5 entered in a different order from the Maker

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Compare with the request. If YOU made the mistake, correct and click 'Run check' again. If the MAKER is wrong, click 'Return to Maker', type the reason, and reply to the Maker's email.

3.2 The CHECK RESULT block - your five answers

Right side of the Checker sheet (columns I-J)

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Select the block (the exact range is written above it), copy, and paste it into your email to the Second Checker.

'Same account and amount more than once'

This is a reminder, not an error. Confirm in the request that both lines are really there (e.g. salary and bonus to the same employee).

3.3 Create the files and email the Second Checker

Files created - DEDSALUPLOA and DEMSALUPLOA

Email 2 - Checker to Second Checker (reply on the same chain)

Subject: RE: Bulk Upload - Payroll Files - Batch 5010 - checked

Dear <Second Checker>,

Attached: original request, DEDSALUPLOA5010, DEMSALUPLOA5010.

<paste the CHECK RESULT block here>

Checker: <name>

4. Internal Transfers - Second Checker (Unit Head)

You do not need the tool. Work from the email chain:

  • The request matches the Checker's answers: number of entries and total amount (Q1, Q2).

  • Open DEMSALUPLOA in Notepad: batch number, branch, today's date, total debit / credit equal Q1 and Q2.

  • Open DEDSALUPLOA in Notepad: number of lines = number of entries; serials 000001 to the last; today's date.

  • Top 3 debit / credit / customer-account amounts look right against the request; any 'same account and amount' lines are in the request.

  • Maker, Checker and you are three different people.

  • Record the batch in the Bulk Upload Register and reply to the approver for approval.

  • After approval, place both files unchanged in DE\OUT; when they disappear, check the journal in ACRPJR.

5. SWIFT Outward - Maker

Upload sheet - after creating the upload and entering the transfers

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Enter the Batch number, No. of transfers and the Request total (from the request).
2 Click 'Create upload'. Exactly that number of lines is created.
3 For each line, select the Beneficiary bank from the list - do not type it.
4 The SWIFT code appears automatically from the bank you selected.
5 The batch reference (e.g. 19181026_01) is filled automatically, in line order.
6 Total of lines must equal the request total: the Difference must be 0.00.
7 Click 'Submit to Checker'.
Column Type Tip
Debit account 051090019411 12 digits, typed as text
Beneficiary name Orange Data Max 60 characters; no comma, no '&'
Beneficiary account 500015110008 WITHOUT '/' - the tool adds it
Beneficiary bank HSBC Bank Egypt Select from the list
Amount 1729.55 1120 becomes 1120.00
Remittance info / POP REF/FAWRY Max 32 characters; no comma
Order-by account 051090019411 Usually the debit account; may be different

Filled by the tool - nothing to type

Transaction date 18102026 | '/' before the beneficiary account | SWIFT code | batch reference | type SAL | blank purpose code

5.1 If something is wrong

Example - leading zero lost from the debit account, comma in the name and in the amount

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Debit account must be 12 digits - the leading 0 was lost. Re-type it.
2 Remove the comma from the beneficiary name.
3 Type the amount as 7187 or 7187.00 - no comma.

5.2 Possible duplicates - override with a reason

If the same beneficiary account receives the same amount more than once, the tool stops and asks you to confirm when you click 'Submit to Checker':

Possible duplicate alert

  1. Check the original request. If each transfer is genuine (e.g. two separate bills), click Yes and type the reason (e.g. 'Two separate bills, ref 123 and 124').

  2. If it is a mistake, click No and correct or remove the line.

  3. The Checker gets the same alert when running the check and must also confirm. Both overrides appear in the CHECK RESULT block.

5.3 Save and email the Checker

  1. File > Save As > working folder > SwiftUpload_<batch>_<date>.xlsm (e.g. SwiftUpload_19_18102026.xlsm).

  2. Email the Checker from Outlook with the request and the workbook location.

Email 4 - Maker to Checker (example)

Subject: SWIFT Outward Bulk Upload - Batch 19 - 18102026 - for checking

Dear <Checker>,

Please check the attached request.

Workbook: <working folder>\SwiftUpload_19_18102026.xlsm

Number of transfers: 6 Total amount: 11,685.90 Debit account: 051090019411

Maker: <name>

6. SWIFT Outward - Checker

Checker sheet - your own entries from the request, after 'Run check'

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Enter all 7 fields of every transfer from the ORIGINAL request, in the same order. Select the bank from the list.
2 Click 'Run check'.
3 Each line shows 'Matched' or 'DIFFERENT: <field>'.
4 When PASSED, click 'Create upload files'.

6.1 The CHECK RESULT block - five answers for outward transfers

An outward upload only debits the customer's account (the credits are at the other banks), so instead of 'debit = credit' the tool answers these five questions:

Right side of the Checker sheet (columns L-M)

Marker What it means / what to do
1 Select the block, copy, and paste it into your email to the Second Checker.
Question What to look at
Q1 Total transfers Count and total agree with the request
Q2 Debit account(s) Normally one account - the customer's account in the request
Q3 Top 3 transfers The largest payments are correct
Q4 By bank The split by bank / SWIFT code makes sense
Q5 Paid more than once Repeated beneficiaries are in the request; 'possible duplicate' lines must be confirmed

If there are possible duplicates, you must confirm them too (same alert as the Maker, with your own reason). The CHECK RESULT then shows both overrides:

Duplicate overrides shown in the final result

6.2 Create the files

Files created

What the SWIFTSAL file looks like - no header, no tabs, comma-separated

Same day only

Create the files on the same day as the check. If the day has changed, return the batch to the Maker to submit again (the date and references are re-stamped).

Email 5 - Checker to Second Checker (reply on the same chain)

Subject: RE: SWIFT Outward Bulk Upload - Batch 19 - 18102026 - checked

Dear <Second Checker>,

Attached: original request, SWIFTSAL 18102026_19.txt, EGYPTSWSAL.txt.

<paste the CHECK RESULT block here>

Checker: <name>

7. SWIFT Outward - Second Checker (Unit Head)

  • The request agrees with Q1 (number of transfers and total) and Q2 (debit account).

  • Open the SWIFTSAL file in Notepad: number of lines = number of transfers; today's date on every line; references from _01 to the last; two commas together before the remittance info (blank purpose code).

  • Review the top 3 transfers (Q3), the bank split (Q4) and repeated beneficiaries (Q5) against the request.

  • If duplicates were overridden, read the Maker and Checker reasons in the result and confirm them against the request.

  • EGYPTSWSAL.txt is present and empty.

  • Maker, Checker and you are three different people.

  • Record the batch in the Bulk Upload Register and send for approval. After approval place both files, unchanged, in the SWIFT shared folder.

  • After processing, the Checker reconciles the debit-account statement; failed transfers need Unit Head approval before manual processing (OEGP).

8. Quick reference

Step Internal Transfers SWIFT Outward
Maker - header Upload type, Branch, Batch, Number of entries Batch, Number of transfers, Request total
Maker - each line Account/GL, Account branch, Narration, D/C, Amount Debit acc, Beneficiary name, Beneficiary acc, Bank, Amount, Remittance, Order-by
Maker - must be true Difference (Dr - Cr) = 0.00 Difference to request total = 0.00
Checker - each line Account/GL, Narration, D/C, Amount All 7 fields
Files created DEDSALUPLOA<batch>, DEMSALUPLOA<batch> SWIFTSAL <date>_<batch>.txt, EGYPTSWSAL.txt
Files placed in DE\OUT SWIFT shared folder
Post-upload check ACRPJR journal Debit-account statement reconciliation

8.1 Messages and what to do

Message What to do
Submission rejected - see column I / L Read the message on each line, correct, submit again
Not balanced / Total does not equal the request total A line is missing, wrong or has the wrong D/C - compare with the request
Account must be ... digits The leading zero was lost or the wrong number was typed - re-type
Account branch must be blank or 3 digits You typed the GL in the branch column - move it to Account / GL
Amount must be like 1500.00 No commas; digits and a dot only
Name / remittance: letters, digits ... only Remove commas, '&' or Arabic text
Beneficiary name longer than 60 / Remittance info longer than 32 Shorten the text - the number in brackets is the current length
POSSIBLE DUPLICATE TRANSFERS Confirm against the request; Yes + reason to override, No to correct
Bank is not in the approved bank list Select the bank from the dropdown; if it is missing, ask your Unit Head / tool owner
You submitted this upload as Maker Another person must check
DIFFERENT: <field> Fix your typing, or Return to Maker if the Maker is wrong
The data changed after the check Click 'Run check' again
Files cannot be created directly in ... Choose the working folder, not the upload folder
'Macros are disabled' page Close, open from the shared folder, click 'Enable Content'

8.2 Frequently asked

Question Answer
Can I add a line after 'Create upload'? No. Start again with 'Create upload' (it asks to clear the batch) and enter the right number of lines.
Can I change the date? No. It is always today.
Does the order of lines matter? Yes - Maker and Checker both follow the order of the request.
Can I email the workbook? No - save it in the shared folder and send the location. Attached macro files are blocked by Outlook / Excel.
Who sends the emails? You do, from Outlook. The tool never sends emails.
